subject: mathematics
question_text: If the vectors a = 2i − j + k, b = i + 2j − 3k and c = 3i + pj + 5k are coplanar, find p.

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IA (2026-27 edition), book p.72, chapter 7 PRODUCT OF VECTORS, Short Answer question 25. Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the Mathematics-IA volume prints no per-step mark allocation on any answer. The split gives half the marks to the determinant and a full mark to the substitution check, because a value of p is only proved once the determinant reads exactly zero. Both evaluations agree at 7p + 28: the first-row expansion gives 2(10 + 3p) + 1(5 + 9) + 1(p − 6), and computing b × c = (10 + 3p, −14, p − 6) and dotting with a gives the same. Substituting p = −4 gives 2(10 − 12) + 1(5 + 9) + 1(−4 − 6) = −4 + 14 − 10 = 0 exactly. Paper position: Maths-1A Section B prints eight short answers of which the student writes any six, each worth 4 marks, under the 2026-27 pattern; Product of Vectors supplies one of them. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

recall_prompt: Say how you would find p — the condition for coplanar vectors, the determinant, and how you check your value.

steps.label: State the condition
steps.margin_note: First mark. Coplanar means the box built on the three vectors is flat, so its volume is zero.
steps.memory_tip: Coplanar means a flat box: zero height, zero volume, zero box product.
lines: Three vectors are coplanar exactly when
their box product is zero, so

recall.must_convey: That coplanar vectors have box product zero, so [a b c] = 0.
accept: coplanar means the scalar triple product is zero
set the box product of the three vectors to zero
a flat box has zero volume, so the determinant is zero
the condition is a b c box product equals zero

steps.why: A non-zero box product is the volume of a real box; if the three vectors lie in one plane that box is flat and the product is zero.
common_mistakes: Setting the box product to 1 instead of 0.
Testing only two of the three vectors for a common plane.

steps.label: Expand the determinant
steps.margin_note: Half the marks. The middle cofactor carries its own minus sign; with a −1 entry that gives a plus.
steps.memory_tip: Two minus signs meet in the middle term: the cofactor's and the entry's. They give a plus.

accept: expand the determinant to get seven p plus twenty eight
b cross c is ten plus three p, minus fourteen, p minus six
dotting with a gives seven p plus twenty eight
determinant expand cheste seven p plus twenty eight vasthundi
the expansion is linear in p

steps.why: Both routes give the same expression in p, which rules out a sign slip in the cofactor pattern.
common_mistakes: Writing −(−1) as −1 in the middle term.

steps.label: Solve for p and check
steps.margin_note: Last mark. One substitution line turns a candidate into a proved answer.
steps.memory_tip: 7p = −28 gives p = −4. Put it back and the determinant must read exactly 0.

recall.must_convey: That 7p + 28 = 0 gives p = −4, and that substituting it makes the determinant zero.
accept: seven p plus twenty eight equals zero so p is minus four
put minus four back and the determinant is exactly zero
p minus four vasthundi, substitute chesi zero ani choodali
solve the linear equation and check the value

steps.why: Substituting the value back is the proof; the determinant comes out exactly zero, not nearly zero.
